title.value: Global Variations in Event-Based Surveillance for Disease Outbreak Detection: Time Series Analysis
title.justification: The analysis focuses on variations in event-based surveillance systems across the globe for the detection of disease outbreaks. This matches the title's mention of 'Global Variations' and 'Time Series Analysis.'
title.quote: Global Variations in Event-Based Surveillance for Disease Outbreak Detection: Time Series Analysis

extractions.description: The paper analyzes the performance of event-based surveillance (EBS) systems used for detecting infectious disease outbreaks globally. It evaluates the systems' sensitivity, specificity, and timeliness in detecting seasonal influenza outbreaks in 24 countries using EBS data from HealthMap and WHO's Epidemic Intelligence from Open Sources (EIOS), compared to virological data from FluNet as a reference. The study identifies the determinants affecting EBS performance and highlights the need for improvements, particularly in resource-limited settings.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper is centered on evaluating infectious disease surveillance systems, which, while important for public health, do not directly address climate change as a primary theme.
climate_change_is_central.quote: The aim of this study was to assess the variation in the timing and frequency of EBS reports compared to true outbreaks and to identify the determinants of variability by using the example of seasonal influenza epidemic in 24 countries.

primary_category.justification: The study does not focus on climate change themes but rather on public health surveillance for infectious diseases.
primary_category.quote: The aim of this study was to assess the variation in the timing and frequency of EBS reports compared to true outbreaks and to identify the determinants of variability by using the example of seasonal influenza epidemic in 24 countries.

secondary_categories.quote: Infectious disease surveillance produces crucial information for public health professionals to make good emergency response decisions and implement effective countermeasures to contain outbreaks.

primary_sub_category.justification: No sub-category aligns with the core focus of public health disease outbreak surveillance discussed in the paper.
primary_sub_category.quote: Event-based surveillance (EBS) was developed to complement IBS to enable near real-time detection of infectious disease outbreaks.

secondary_sub_categories.quote: Infectious diseases continue to threaten populations worldwide, as demonstrated clearly during the novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 pandemic.

applications.justification: There are no specific applications related to climate change in this study, as it centers on disease outbreak detection capabilities of public health systems rather than environmental policy or climate interventions.
applications.quote: Overall, while monitoring the frequency of EBS reports over 7 years in 24 countries, we detected 175 out of 238 outbreaks (73.5%).
